question: The certification post from emit (32f500e517d7) puts a socket on the inspector's verdict path, which the fire-path rule forbids. Which yields: (a) the rule narrows so a fire-and-forget post is allowed and only a consult (tree, database, a host that answers) is denied; (b) emit stops posting and the certification is posted by something off the verdict path; or (c) something else?
why_it_blocks: test_inspector_nexus test_the_fire_path_never_reaches_the_tree and the fire_path_unreachable sieve are red at HEAD (measured: same red with this build reverted). Path: inspector -> transitions -> gate_probes -> bus_client.remote (socket), added by 32f500e517d7 (4cb79062), whose D2 argued the post 'never decides a verdict'; 48519f4789b1 D14 had removed an earlier emit bus post for exactly this reason. Measured: cutting transitions->gate_probes or gate_probes->remote each clears it; transitions is reached from inspector by 8 other modules, so splitting the grammar out is large; a dynamic import or subprocess would only hide the edge. 339a45cee6a1's falsifier needs every build_inspector proof green, so its PROVED waits on this.
answer: Neither (a) nor (b). Akien 2026-10-27: 'so we should simplify that a lot. the inspector does all the checks. so there is no need for more checks. the idea was make one file type you can't write. then add a cyptographic or similar way to say that the right code wrote the certificate on this date at this time with these hashed findings. that's a thing that should be in the base gate class. the reason for entry gates was just so we could kick things back that didn't meet the entry requirements. nothing in there about who writes what.' / 'the inspectors output is consumed by the gate. the gate's output is the certificate.' / 'the inspector outputs only the findings.' / 'yes, record it and cast the simplification ticket.' The inspector stops reaching emit; the simplification ticket implements it (outline 17.1.1, 19.14.1-19.14.5).
